faq.q: How much does it cost to hire a marketing manager in the UK?
faq.a: Expect the real cost to be 35–45% above the salary. A £30,000 content manager costs about £51,000 a year once National Insurance, pension, recruitment, tools and training are included.

faq.q: Is outsourcing marketing cheaper than hiring in-house?
faq.a: For most small businesses, yes. In-house teams tend to become more cost-efficient only once marketing spend passes roughly £120,000–£150,000 a year.

faq.q: How much does a marketing agency cost per month in the UK?
faq.a: Specialist agencies typically charge £2,000–£5,000 a month for one channel, content agencies £5,000–£10,000, and full-service agencies £12,000–£25,000 or more.

faq.q: What is a productised marketing service?
faq.a: A service sold like a product: fixed deliverables at a fixed monthly price, rather than hours or open-ended retainers. It suits small businesses that want predictable costs.

faq.q: What is a hybrid marketing model?
faq.a: One person inside the business owns marketing and decisions, while outside specialists do the execution. Many growing UK SMEs use it.

faq.q: Can a small business have a full marketing team for under £500 a month?
faq.a: Yes, with a productised service. The ContentFellow Growth Fellow covers shoots, editing, social, website and search for £389 a month.
